description: Discriminator: with the transitive-skip flag on, does executing a committed instance whose command commutes with its uncommitted dependency succeed, or does it wait for that dependency as if the flag were off? Prefix: the harness builds the two records with the package's own constructors and calls the executor's entry for the committed instance. Controls: the prerequisite prints the flag, both statuses and that the two commands commute, and the result prints whether execution happened and the statuses afterwards.

harness.description: In-package Go test that prepares a commuting uncommitted dependency and asks the real executor to run the committed instance with the flag set.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: the Replica is constructed in-package with the flag set and the two records are built directly with the package's types
the harness calls the executor entry directly instead of the execution loop

legality.derivation: The flag is set exactly as a caller would through epaxos.New, and the records are the states a replica reaches (one committed with a dependency on one uncommitted instance).
legality.applicability: One replica, two records, flag on.
unresolved: the soundness of skipping is out of scope

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the executor ran the instance and the statuses afterwards, which is the observable of the documented skipping.
grounding.applicability: The flag was on and the commands commute.

observable_properties.description: With transitive-conflict skipping enabled, execution must not wait for a prior command it commutes with.

uncertainties: the check does not establish whether skipping is sound in general, only whether the documented behaviour occurs
the flag is false in the shipped configuration
